deck_context.source_summary: FinPilot is an English/Chinese finance education chatbot using FastAPI, local calculators, lexical RAG and DeepSeek. Homepage React/TypeScript with GSAP/Motion; workspace native JS/CSS. Current companion uses reused 2D WebP atlases and Canvas2D on web and Electron desktop, explicit shared session over SQLite/SSE.
deck_context.core_claim: Make financial explanations traceable and usable, with an interactive companion that preserves the same evidence.
deck_context.factual_limits: Do not claim trained RAG, embeddings, vector database, market prediction, all-React architecture, new 3D avatar, phoneme lip sync or full v15 end-to-end acceptance. Illustrations of interfaces are conceptual diagrams, not screenshots.

slides.title: Reliable grounding needs more than retrieval
slides.intent: Explain two RAG challenges and concrete responses while admitting the rule-check limit.

layout.composition: Two broad side-by-side illustrated challenges below a two-line headline. Left: English and Chinese term slips feeding a search/index mechanism. Right: a claim sheet checked against a source book with a magnifying glass. Each side has its challenge heading and exactly one solution line. Bottom a slim mustard strip contains Missing values stay missing; underneath a modest but clearly readable limitation. No architecture repeated from sample; avoid tiny footnotes.

visual_elements.main_visual: Retro flat filing drawer and small bilingual word slips on left; evidence inspection on right. Do not add illegible fake paragraphs.

local_context.background: Both retrieval routes are lexical. Chinese n-grams and BM25 rankings use RRF. Citation support checking is limited rule-based topic checking with at most one repair. Missing local data must not become zero.

constraints: Use exact English key points only. Do not add Chinese vocabulary examples. Do not display the retrieval metric on this slide; it belongs in notes and Q&A.

slides.title: Frontend design keeps complex tasks usable
slides.intent: Explain responsive hierarchy, resilient motion and asynchronous state through paired concise copy.

layout.composition: Large headline on two lines at top, left side a flat outlined desktop screen with a phone partially beside it, as conceptual wireframes with clean shapes and no fake text. Right side three vertically separated rows with medium large headings and one short solution line each. Use colored simple icons to distinguish hierarchy, motion and request order. Single small but readable tech-stack line at bottom. Do not reproduce cards or source diagram.

visual_elements.main_visual: Desktop and phone conceptual interface showing the same chat/input and collapsed assistant, with visually clear spacing. A small poster icon and a pair of orderly numbered messages in supporting row icons.

local_context.background: Actual homepage uses React/TypeScript/Vite and GSAP/Motion. Workspace is vanilla JavaScript/CSS. Hero video falls back to a poster; reduced motion is respected. Request IDs/cancellation prevent old calculations overwriting new input, chat failure retains draft.

constraints: Visible wording exactly as key points. Do not label the whole application React. Do not claim speed or user-retention improvements.

slides.intent: Show explicit session selection, persisted state and stale-result filtering, then close the talk.
key_points: One saved conversation with the same evidence.

layout.composition: A closing architectural postcard different from sample. At center a large shared conversation ledger with SQLite + SSE and Save, notify, reload underneath. To its left a web browser window with heading Web workspace and caption Choose one session. To right a desktop chat panel with heading Desktop companion and caption Reject stale responses.
